text: Open on the whole subject within the first 2 s (the hook) and end on a still hero framing held at least 1.5 s.
The studied ads run {stat:all.shotsPer10s.median} shots per 10 s. Stay within 3-7 per 10 s: calm (3-5) for furniture and rooms, medium (4-6) for products, hype (5-7) for vehicles.
fallbackText: Use 3-7 shots per 10 s: calm (3-5) for furniture and rooms, medium (4-6) for products, hype (5-7) for vehicles.

text: At every cut, change the camera angle by at least 30 degrees or the subject's size on screen by 1.5x. Alternating full frames and detail shots does this naturally.
Every clip has at least one macro_detail shot on the subject's best detail or on a user marker, filling most of the frame.
Never a turntable. arc_orbit sweeps 20-90 degrees with easing; the subject stays still unless a motion block moves it.
Every move eases in and out, and the last shot settles into true stillness (settleFrac 0.3-0.5 on the hero).
Small products: 85-135 mm on details, 50-85 mm on full frames, f/2-4 for shallow focus, and a rim that draws the silhouette.

Glossy subjects (glossShare 0.2 or more on the subject card) get reflection_rig: one big soft plane and controlled black elsewhere (darkShare 0.4-0.7). Three-point softboxes make blob highlights on gloss.

Matte, fabric and textured subjects get softbox_three_point: key 15-45 degrees off the camera and above it, fillRatio 0.25-0.5 (key:fill 2:1 to 4:1), rim on. A raking light shows texture on the detail shot.
Vehicles: full frames at 28 mm or longer (never wide and close), a low front three-quarter hero, and f/5.6 or higher on full frames so the whole car is sharp (anti-miniature).
Vehicle detail shots go to the lamps first, then the badge, a wheel, the shoulder line.
A dark studio sells a car: studio_cyc tone black with a low lowerHemisphereGain, a rim over the roofline, haze 0.4-0.8 for depth.
Furniture: calm pace, camera near eye height with verticals straight (elevation 0-15 degrees), a top-weighted key (keyElevationDeg 50-70), and a raking side light on the texture detail.
Characters and figures: when the figure is still, the camera performs (push, arc); put a detail shot on the face; key off-axis with a motivated rim.

Grade by mood: premium_dark or noir for luxury and night, clean or vivid for playful and bright, warm_golden for warm and sunset asks, teal_night for neon and night-city asks. Keep separation 1.10-1.20 so the subject stands out.
Atmosphere carries realism: light haze (0.1-0.3) on studio products, heavier (0.4-0.8) for moody cars and night looks; keep clearPocket on.
The reference ads favour a low camera for heroes. Camera heights observed: {stat:all.cameraHeight}.
fallbackText: The owner's reference ads favour a low camera for heroes; low_hero_push with heightFrac 0.05-0.2 is the default hook.

text: Vague prompts: decide boldly from the direction. A neutral grey studio with one slow orbit is the failure, not the safe choice.
Markers are the spots the user cares about: give each marker its own macro_detail shot (target {marker: id}) in marker order, near its timeS when one is given, and follow its text as a creative wish.

When the prompt asks for something the menu cannot build (rain, a street, driving, text, music), get as close as the menu allows (a night grade for 'rainy night', a warm grade for 'sunset') and list the ask in unsupported.
9:16 is the default: angles that read vertically (low hero, three-quarter) beat flat side profiles, and the subject stays in the middle of the frame.
Studied vehicle ads cut every {stat:vehicle.shotLenS.median} s (median shot length).
fallbackText: Vehicle ads cut every 0.75-2.5 s: the owner's F40 reference holds about 2.5 s a shot, the M4 chase about 0.75 s.

text: If the subject card lists animationClips and the prompt asks for movement (walks, dances, waves), use motion play_clip with the clip whose untrusted name fits best, else the longest clip. Keep the camera moves calm so the performance reads.

Wind is one field for the whole clip. Leave it still indoors. Outdoors, a light breeze (2-4 m/s) makes grass, fog and rain feel alive; set 6-10 m/s only when the prompt asks for wind or a storm. Never put wind on a single effect.
Low fog sells scale and night: 0.3-0.6 m on streets and fields, kept out of a clear pocket around the subject. Use mist (not fog) for dawn and overcast. Never fog plus heavy haze in one clip.
Finish like film, lightly: halation 0.2-0.4 on night and neon moods, grain 0.2-0.4 on everything except clean catalogue looks, lens distortion at most 0.006 and never on product close-ups.

rain_courtyard is the cinematic outdoor default for vehicles and large objects: low hero angles, wet asphalt, overcast or dusk. Small products look lost in it unless the camera stays low and close (macro_detail, low_hero_push at 50 mm or longer).

Rain reads only against light: keep a light behind or beside the subject (rim or practicals). Drizzle for products and calm moods, steady for most, downpour only for vehicles and hype. Rain means wet: the ground and subject get wet automatically.
After the rain beats rain for products: wet ground and calm puddles that mirror the subject, no falling drops. Streets at night: wetness 0.6-1.0.
Droplets are a freshness cue: 1-2 mm on glass and glossy paint, sparse on matte. With rain they come automatically; alone they say 'ice-cold' or 'morning dew'.
Snow is quiet: calm pace, cool or neutral grade, light wind. Accumulation 3-10 mm reads real; more buries detail. Never snow and rain together.
Lens drops are a cliche used once: at most one non-detail shot, only in rain, amount 0.2-0.4.

night_street is the neon/night world: rim_neon (reflection_rig for gloss) with the street's practicals, never a studio softbox. Wet ground (0.6-1.0) doubles every light in reflections. Low camera, 28-50 mm for vehicles, 50-85 mm for products.

golden_field is warm and quiet: hard_sun (reflection_rig for gloss), sun 2-15 degrees behind or beside the subject for a rim, calm or medium pace, warm_golden grade. A breeze (2-4 m/s) keeps the grass alive; still air looks like a photo.
Overcast courtyards light from the sky alone (hdri_only, a light negative fill for shape); add a rim only for gloss. A dusk courtyard takes hard_sun.
Small products can arrive by drop-in: 0.4-0.8 of their height, one soft bounce, slowed to 0.4-0.5 so the weight reads. The camera holds still or pushes gently during the landing.

Floating is for tech and luxury small objects: slow bob, a few degrees of yaw per second. A plinth spin is one eased quarter-to-half turn while the camera also moves. Never a full constant spin (that is a T1 turntable).
A slide-in is a clean product entrance: short, decelerating to a crisp stop, then hold. Enter across the frame, never toward the camera.

Rolls and topples are playful entrances for round or tall products; they end in a held rest, then the camera finds the hero angle. Keep a roll short enough to stay in frame; never roll a shape that isn't round.
Toss-and-tumble is high energy: hype pace, one clean spin, slowed to 0.4-0.5, landing into a hold.

Cars drive with intent: a straight pass or a gentle arc at 30-60 km/h on a street, courtyard or field, framed by a low anchor camera the car passes (or a tracking camera). Brake to a stop and hold for the hero. Never drive in the studio.
reveal_rise lands a middle or final shot: it starts on a detail and rises to the whole subject. Use it once. Good after a drop-in or at the end of a slide.
A dutch angle is a hype accent: one shot, 8-15 degrees, never the opener or the hero landing.
Handheld gives life to street and courtyard scenes: shake 0.2-0.4, walk around the subject. Not for clean studio product shots, and never with a dutch shot in the same clip.
Side slides show a vehicle's or product's silhouette; add a foreground layer outdoors for depth.
